rewrite.hint: The name is borrowed from POSIX, but Node’s version does not duplicate the running program. Ask what it starts instead.
rewrite.explanation: child_process.fork(modulePath) is spawn specialized for Node: it starts a brand-new node process running the module you name — fresh memory, its own event loop, a different pid — and wires up an IPC channel so parent and child can exchange messages. Despite the name it is not POSIX fork(2): none of the parent’s memory is copied and the child begins at the first line of your module. It is not a thread either (that is worker_threads, which shares the process) and it does not go through a shell (that is exec).

rewrite.hint: Two processes have separate memory, so nothing can be handed over by reference. Ask what form the data has to take to cross between them.
rewrite.explanation: A forked child has its own memory, so the two sides exchange copies: the parent calls child.send(value), the child calls process.send(value), and each side receives the other’s messages through a "message" event — process.on("message") in the child, child.on("message") in the parent. Values are serialized, so functions and class instances do not survive the trip and mutating the object you sent changes nothing on the other side. Shared variables and global state cannot reach across a process boundary at all, and while argv can carry startup data it is one-way and fixed at launch.

rewrite.hint: exec keeps everything the child prints until it exits. Ask what has to give when that pile outgrows the limit Node puts on it.
rewrite.explanation: exec holds all of stdout and stderr in memory until the child exits, bounded by the maxBuffer option, which defaults to 1 MiB. When the child writes past it Node terminates the child and calls your callback with an error whose code is ERR_CHILD_PROCESS_STDIO_MAXBUFFER — it does not truncate silently and it does not spill to a file, so a command that behaves in testing starts failing once a log or a directory listing grows. Raising maxBuffer only moves the ceiling; for output of unknown size use spawn and read the stream as it arrives.
